headline.one_liner: Fifteen data centers within five miles are on your local grid, served by Dominion Energy. A typical home here pays about $31 more a month than two years ago.

on_your_grid.summary: Fifteen data-center facilities sit within five miles, nine of them within one mile. All are served by Dominion Energy, the utility that serves your street. The eight Northgate buildings are likely fed from the same 230 kV substation as your neighborhood; that is inferred from distance, not from utility records.

sources.title: Utility service territory map (fictional)
sources.quote: Dominion Energy Virginia: Loudoun County east of Route 15

coming.summary: Within five miles, 59 acres of open land became data-center roof between the 2023 and 2025 imagery, taking the total from 112 to 171 acres. One 23-acre site 1.4 miles north of you is in no facility database.

your_bill.summary: Your state's average residential price rose 22.8% over 24 months. For a home using 1,100 kWh a month that is about $31 more per month, between $25 and $37 depending on how much you use. The regional market monitor attributes most of the latest capacity-price increase to data-center load.

sources.title: State residential price series (fictional)
sources.quote: Average residential price, VA, Aug 2026: 15.1 c/kWh; Aug 2024: 12.3 c/kWh

sources.title: Regional market monitor report (fictional)
sources.quote: 63% of the capacity price increase is attributable to data center load

price.attribution: 63% of the capacity price increase is attributable to data center load (market monitor, fictional)

protection.summary: Partly. A large-load tariff is in force: customers above 25 MW pay for their own transmission upgrades, so that part of the build-out is kept off your bill. It does not shield you from capacity prices, which every customer pays and which the market monitor says are rising with data-center load.

sources.title: Commission order, large-load tariff (fictional)
sources.quote: Customers with demand above 25 MW shall bear the incremental cost of transmission upgrades

sources.title: Regional market monitor report (fictional)
sources.quote: 63% of the capacity price increase is attributable to data center load

hearing.summary: The Board of Supervisors votes on the Broad Run rezoning on 12 November. At the last meeting a supervisor said no further campus would be approved on that substation without a capacity study.
